extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of Milton and early-modern English; editors and annotators of historical texts
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly explanatory notes and glosses for Milton's Areopagitica: etymologies, textual variants, citations, definitions, and contextual/biographical remarks to support a critical edition or classroom reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain bracketed editorial queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to bracketed prompts in the notes (e.g. '[4. Explain the rending, not the vanity^]', '[24. Explain collated.]', '[3. Explain tabrd here.]', '[25. Explain practiz'd the books]') by supplying concise explanations or expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the editor has inserted bracketed 'Explain ...' queries, provide the requested gloss, historical sense, or textual clarification; show the passage in context and give any necessary citations or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide etymologies and word‑origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace the derivation of words used in the text (e.g. 'Seize is from the Fr. saiser, which is from the Low Lat. sacire, which is from the O. H. G. sazjan', 'scurrill. Milton seems to have used this form ...', 'cautelous is from Lat. cautela').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the language-of-origin chain, related historical forms, and relevant reference works (e.g. Brachet, Diez, Nares, Richardson) and illustrate usage with dated examples when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and cite textual variants and emendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Note variant readings between editions/manuscripts and any emendations (e.g. the 1644 reading 'wayfaring' vs 'warfaring'; Milton's own copy where 'y' is crossed out and 'r' written above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document manuscript or edition evidence for variants, state who made the change, provide provenance (press-mark, owner), and give an assessment whether the change is warranted or an improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain obsolete spellings, grammatical forms, and archaic usages
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify forms and senses no longer current (e.g. 'ancienter', Elizabethan comparatives/adverbial superlatives, 'hath bin explaining' as a gerundal verbal substantive, 'want' = 'be without').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the grammatical category or historical sense, compare with modern equivalents, cite grammars or specimen collections (Morris, Skeat, Morris's English Accidence) and give dated textual examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give bibliographic references and secondary literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply supporting references to editions and scholarly works (e.g. 'See Hallam's Literature of Europe', 'See Smith's Bible Dict.', 'See Milner's Gallery of Geography').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting historical, biographical, or interpretive claims, provide full citations (author, work, volume/page when available) so readers can verify and follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concise biographical and historical context for persons and places
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify historical figures and give dates/roles (e.g. 'Eusebius, born circ. 264... chosen Bishop of Caesarea circ. 315', 'Selden was born 1584, died 1654'), and contextualize references (e.g. Sorbonne's role).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer brief life-dates, offices, and why the person/place matters for understanding the passage; include pointers to fuller biographies or standard histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and cite quoted passages and parallels
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate and cite passages quoted or alluded to (Biblical references, Paradise Lost lines, Shakespeare, Horace, Aristotle, etc.) with book/chapter/line or edition references (e.g. 'See Matthew xv. 17-20; Mark vii. 14-23', 'Paradise Lost, xi. 530-538').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise citations for quotations and parallels, indicate edition or translation where necessary, and show the quotation's relevance to the note or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify semantic distinctions between related terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain fine meaning differences (e.g. 'theorems. We commonly use 'theory' with this meaning; but strictly 'theory' is abstract, 'theorem' is concrete, as in Euclid').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the strict sense vs. common modern usage, provide examples illustrating the distinction, and if applicable, cite authoritative sources or classical usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note orthographic and typographical corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out and correct printing or spelling errors and note correct orthography (e.g. 'There should be no g in the word 'forain' [forain = foraine] ; the 'forain' is from the Lat. foraneus').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the incorrect printed form, give the corrected form, explain the derivation if relevant, and supply comparative instances from other period texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide original‑language citations and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Latin/Greek quotations or original-language forms with translations or glosses when they occur (e.g. Greek lines from Homer, Latin citations from Cicero, Tacitus, and Defensio Secunda Latin excerpt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply the original text (transliterated when appropriate), give an English translation or gloss, and cite the classical source and book/line numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gloss rare, technical, or dialectal words with historical examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Define specialized or uncommon vocabulary (e.g. 'ribald', 'repasting', 'viands', 'cautelous', 'excremental') and show period examples of usage (Shakespeare, Pope, Nares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer derivation, sense(s) in Milton's time, and attestations from contemporary authors or glossaries; cite the lexicographical source used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross‑reference related passages within the edition and external texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Point readers to other notes, other works by Milton, and parallel passages across literature (e.g. 'See Paradise Lost, iii. 543-554', 'Cp. Bishop Hall's Contemplations' , 'See Longer English Poems').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide internal page/note references and external work citations so readers can follow the chain of allusion or variant discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make evaluative judgments about readings and interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: When relevant, assess interpretive choices (e.g. 'That the change is certainly an improvement. The context, I think, makes clear.'), evaluating whether an emendation or interpretation is preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the grounds for the judgment (contextual, manuscript evidence, usage parallels), and where possible offer alternatives and reasons for choosing one reading over another.
